title: AI Models for Application Development and Evaluation
description: Explore AI models for text, images, and other supported inputs and outputs. Compare task fit, model documentation, deployment requirements, and license terms.
introduction: AI models are the underlying systems used to interpret inputs or produce outputs in applications. This category includes model resources rather than only finished chat interfaces or task-specific editors. Entries may differ in supported modalities, deployment options, and access to model files. Start with a well-defined task and representative evaluation material. Developer APIs is more relevant when choosing a hosted integration, while AI Chatbot focuses on an end-user conversational experience built around one or more models.
capabilities: Process the input and output types documented for the specific model and release.
Support application tasks through available hosted access or compatible model deployment workflows.
Provide a basis for task-specific evaluation using representative prompts and reference outcomes.
Allow supported adaptation or configuration where the release and its terms permit those changes.

audiences.label: Application teams
audiences.text: Evaluate a model against a defined product task, then test it within the intended user workflow.

audiences.label: Researchers and platform engineers
audiences.text: Inspect model documentation, reproduce relevant evaluations, and assess deployment and maintenance requirements before adoption.

criteria.label: Task evidence
criteria.text: Read intended uses, limitations, language coverage, and evaluation conditions before testing your own representative examples.

criteria.label: Deployment requirements
criteria.text: Check compatible software, hardware needs, latency, and operational effort for the access method you intend to use.

criteria.label: Release terms
criteria.text: Review the actual model license, version, and restrictions rather than inferring permissions from download availability.

workflow: Define the task, acceptable outputs, difficult cases, and constraints for the intended application.
Review documentation and evaluate the exact model release using a representative, repeatable set of examples.
Test the chosen deployment path and record version, configuration, limitations, and operating requirements.

faqs.question: How is a model different from a chatbot?
faqs.answer: A model provides underlying processing or generation capability. A chatbot adds a conversational interface and surrounding product features, which may include files, search, tools, or several models used for different purposes.

faqs.question: Does a downloadable model permit every commercial use?
faqs.answer: Do not infer permissions from download access. Read the specific release license and associated conditions, including any restrictions on use, modification, or distribution, before choosing it for a commercial application.

faqs.question: What should I look for in a model card?
faqs.answer: Look for intended tasks, limitations, supported languages, evaluation results, and information about training and use. Treat the documentation as a starting point and verify the properties that matter in your application.

faqs.question: Can benchmark results replace testing on our own tasks?
faqs.answer: Benchmarks help describe performance under particular conditions, but your inputs and success criteria may differ. Evaluate representative examples, including difficult cases, before assuming a reported score predicts the product experience.

faqs.question: Why should I record the exact model version?
faqs.answer: A release change can alter behavior, compatibility, or operational requirements. Recording the version and configuration makes evaluation results easier to interpret and helps the team compare changes when updating a deployment.
